\begin{frame}{Excel date parsing example}
\small
A practical part of the original exploration was helping users turn exported date strings into usable Excel dates before any KPI work could start.

\vspace{0.4em}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Clean export}
{\ttfamily\scriptsize =IF(A2=0,"",DATE(LEFT(TEXT(A2,"00000000"),4),\\
 MID(TEXT(A2,"00000000"),5,2),\\
 RIGHT(TEXT(A2,"00000000"),2)))}
\column{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Mixed export}
{\ttfamily\scriptsize =IF(A2="","",IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("/",A2)),\\
 DATE(MID(A2,FIND("/",A2,FIND("/",A2)+1)+1,4),\\
 LEFT(A2,FIND("/",A2)-1),\\
 MID(A2,FIND("/",A2)+1,FIND("/",A2,FIND("/",A2)+1)-FIND("/",A2)-1)),\\
 DATE(RIGHT(LEFT(A2,10),4),MID(A2,4,2),LEFT(A2,2))))}
\end{columns}

{\scriptsize The Python pipeline now uses the same logic. The Excel formulas stay here as documentation of the exploration, not as the source of truth.}
\end{frame}
